item.title: New Season Upgrades Vol 4: Fish, Ghostty and Way Too Many Fonts
item.description:
Volume 3 left me typing at the speed of a concerned grandparent. Though I probably should leave it at that, I added even more changes :D The following upgrades are not too demanding on muscle memory, though, rather they remove some clutter that has been building up.

TL;DR: I replaced my shell. And my terminal. And my font. (Fonts, actually, plural. We’ll get to that. 😅)

zsh -> fish (again) Link to heading

Like Protonmail in Volume 1, this one’s a homecoming. My dotfiles still had a .config/fish folder full of dusty functions from last time.

item.title: New Season Upgrades Vol 3: Split Keyboard Adventures!
item.description: Sorry, all: This blog post is long overdue. In fact any post at all is overdue at this point; suffice it to say it’s been a while. The not-so-relevant-for-this-blog reason behind this is mainly that we’re fixing the foundation drainage on our wonderful new house these days, and it takes quite a lot of time. A house built on solid rock is definitely by The Book, but it also presents some interesting challenges in that the machines can’t necessarily reach where all the digging needs to be done. Hm. Perhaps there’s a relevant lesson there after all? In any case, I’m digging and moving heavy rocks more than most, and definitely more than I’m blogging. Never slept deeper nor been in better physical shape, though! Makes the local gym feel like a lazy SPA spa.

item.title: New Season Upgrades Vol 2: New Newsletter Platform!
item.description:
The migration season continues! In Volume 1 I finally moved my incoming mail from Gmail to Protonmail. Today it’s the outgoing kind: the newsletter (that thing that pings you whenever I post here) is moving to Buttondown.

The old setup was follow.it, and to be fair, it did its job. Emails went out, people got them. But it never felt like something I’d pick twice, and rather than listing my grievances I’ll just show you the old subscribe form that lived at the bottom of this very page:

item.title: New Season Upgrades Vol 1: from Gmail to Protonmail (again)
item.description: What a time to be alive. Elm has had numerous “native” versions lately (Eco and elm-run, the latter of which I’ve blogged about already), and I’m happy to say I’m testing the more “official” Acadia alpha. And there’s a new Elm version, with another one coming up shortly as well. All (mostly anyway) while I was either in the middle of MOVING from Askim to Skien, and/or on my glorious and long Lofoten vacation with my family.
